title: Pattern's Maple conduit throttles deposits but leaves withdrawals unlimited
content:
The Maple USDC instance configures its two directions asymmetrically. Inflow: "`maxAmount`: 100,000,000 USDC, `slope`: 20,000,000 USDC per day" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.4.1). Outflow: "`maxAmount`: Unlimited" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.4.2).

The principle this expresses is that a rate limit is a control on **building exposure**, not on unwinding it. Throttling entry bounds how fast the Agent can concentrate capital in one counterparty and gives observers time to react to a mistake. Throttling exit would do the opposite of protecting anyone: in a stress event the limit would trap capital inside a failing venue and convert a credit problem into a liquidity problem.

The asymmetry also matches the ecosystem-level design seen elsewhere in the Liquidity Layer, where burning USDS restores mint capacity rather than consuming a separate allowance. In both cases the reversing action is deliberately unconstrained.

One caveat is worth holding onto: an unlimited *contract-level* withdrawal limit does not make exit instant, because Maple redemptions are asynchronous and settle only when the vault processes them. The unlimited setting removes Pattern's own brake on exit; it does not remove the counterparty's. The protection is therefore against self-inflicted delay, not against illiquidity at the venue.
description: Inflow is capped at 100,000,000 USDC with a 20,000,000 per day slope while the withdrawal maxAmount is 'Unlimited' — rate limits govern risk accumulation, never the ability to exit.
